We report results in dollars per participating vehicle-year ($/veh-yr), in absolute dollars, and as a percentage of the unmanaged scenario’s production costs. Production costs include fuel, start and shutdown costs, variable operations and maintenance costs, and a $45/metric ton of CO price on emissions (Bloom et al. 2 2022). All costs except for the start and shutdown costs of non-quick-start generators, which are taken from the Stage 1 day-ahead simulations, are pulled from the Stage 2 real-time simulations. Unlike previous work (Hale et al. 2022a), we do not estimate capacity value. 10 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3 Results The results provide a detailed picture of the pros and cons of RTP, TOU, and DLC as EVMC dispatch mechanisms at different levels of participation (from 2.5% to 45% of LDVs) and with different levels of charge scheduling flexibility (within-session and within-week). We examine the value of the mechanisms with perfect-foresight in Section 3.1, examine the value of perfect- foresight compared to no-foresight, i.e., forecast value, in Section 3.2, describe implementation challenges associated with RTP in Section 3.3, and consider the value of price-responsive mechanisms compared to DLC, given the additional complexity and costs associated with implementing DLC, in Section 3.4. A full table of results is available in Appendix C. 3.1 Production Cost Savings of Price-Responsive Mechanisms Perfect-foresight provides production cost savings at higher participation rates than the same load integrated with no-foresight. Even with perfect-foresight, there is a maximum participation rate beyond which price-responsive charging provides low or negative savings. Perfect-foresight of price-responsive EV load increases the participation rates at which price- responsive mechanisms produce production cost savings comparable to or better than those achieved by DLC. As in our previous study (Hale et al. 2022a), in this study (Table A.2) we find negative or low savings (less than 35% of DLC’s per-vehicle value) for 14% of LDVs scheduling within-session or within-week charging on an RTP or TOU rate and integrated into grid operations with no-foresight (from −$96/vehicle-yr for within-week RTP to $12/vehicle-yr for within-session TOU compared to $31/vehicle-yr for within-session DLC and $60/vehicle-yr for within-week DLC). Incorporating perfect-foresight of price-responsive EV load changes this result. Figure 2 shows price-responsive mechanisms can yield positive production cost savings for all studied participation rates (up to 45% of LDVs) when scheduling within-session flexibility. For within-week flexibility, 14% to 27% of LDVs responding to RTP or TOU rates provide per-vehicle production cost savings similar to those achieved by DLC (Figure 2). Although foresight greatly increases the relative savings of price-responsive dispatch, there is still a maximum amount of participation beyond which more coordinated DLC mechanisms are necessary to achieve production cost savings. In our simulations, perfect-foresight of RTP or TOU response is insufficient to obtain significant savings from within-week EVMC with 45% of LDVs responding.
